title: Trump Shares Tom Cotton’s Phone Number, Calls for Permanent Daylight Saving Time】
body:
Donald Trump took to his social‑media platform on Saturday to publicly urge Senator Tom Cotton of Arkansas to back a pending piece of legislation that would make daylight‑saving time (DST) permanent across the United States. In the post, the former president not only praised Cotton as “a friend of mine” but also included the senator’s phone number, inviting supporters to contact the lawmaker directly and pressure him to vote for the measure. The move has sparked a flurry of reactions from lawmakers, advocacy groups and the public, highlighting the enduring influence of Trump’s political brand even after his exit from the White House.

The proposal at the center of the controversy is a bipartisan effort to eliminate the bi‑annual clock change that has been a fixture of American life since the Uniform Time Act of 1966. Proponents argue that a year‑round “summer time” would reduce energy consumption, lower traffic accidents, and improve overall public health by providing more evening daylight. Opponents counter that permanent DST would push sunrise later in the winter, leaving many commuters and schoolchildren in darkness during morning hours, and that any change should be decided by Congress rather than through executive or celebrity pressure.

Trump’s public endorsement of the bill is notable for several reasons. First, it underscores his continued willingness to intervene in policy debates that align with his personal preferences—he has long expressed a fondness for the extended daylight evenings that DST provides. Second, by broadcasting Cotton’s direct line, Trump effectively turned a routine legislative effort into a viral campaign, encouraging his millions of followers to flood the senator’s office with calls, texts and emails. Political analysts note that this tactic mirrors past instances where Trump used his platform to mobilize grassroots pressure on specific votes, from judicial nominations to trade legislation.

Senator Cotton, a staunch ally of Trump during the 2020 election cycle, has been a vocal advocate for the “Sunshine Protection Act,” which currently sits in the Senate but faces an uncertain path to passage. While Cotton has previously indicated support for making DST permanent, he has also cautioned that any change would require careful consideration of regional differences and the preferences of constituents in states that span multiple time zones. The sudden influx of public contact spurred by Trump’s post could both bolster Cotton’s resolve and create political backlash if constituents feel harassed or if the outreach is perceived as an intrusion into the legislative process.

Advocacy organizations on both sides of the issue have seized upon the incident to amplify their messages. Consumer‑rights groups warn that permanent DST could disrupt sleep patterns and exacerbate health concerns, especially for children and the elderly. Conversely, business chambers and tourism boards highlight potential economic gains from longer evening daylight, such as increased retail sales and outdoor recreation. The debate has also entered the realm of state politics, with several governors and legislatures already exploring independent moves to adopt year‑round DST or to stay on standard time, further complicating the federal effort.

As the Senate prepares for its upcoming calendar, the episode illustrates how former presidents can still shape policy discourse through direct appeals to lawmakers and the public. Whether Trump’s unorthodox outreach will translate into a decisive vote for the Sunshine Protection Act remains to be seen, but the episode has already heightened visibility for the issue and forced lawmakers to confront a surge of constituent communication. If the bill does advance, it could set a precedent for future attempts to overhaul long‑standing national standards via popular pressure, a dynamic that may redefine how policy is debated in an era of instant digital activism.
